preconditions.description: The number of files to delete (m) is at least 1 and at most the total number of files (n), which is at most 100.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i <= n for a_i in a_indices) and len(set(a_indices)) == m
preconditions.description: The indices of files to delete (a_indices) are distinct, within bounds, and exactly m in number.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(filename) <= 100 for filename in filenames) and all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789.' for filename in filenames for c in filename)
preconditions.description: Each filename is a non-empty string of length at most 100, containing only lowercase letters, digits, or dots.
The total number of filenames provided is exactly n.

postconditions.description: Output is either 'No' (no valid pattern exists) or 'Yes' followed by a valid pattern on the next line.

postconditions.expression: stdout == 'No' or (stdout.splitlines()[0] == 'Yes' and all(len(pattern) == len(filename) for filename in filenames_to_delete) and all(any(pattern[i] == '?' or pattern[i] == filename[i] for i in range(len(filename))) for filename in filenames_to_delete) and all(not (len(pattern) == len(filename) and all(pattern[i] == '?' or pattern[i] == filename[i] for i in range(len(filename)))) for filename in filenames_to_keep))
postconditions.description: If 'Yes' is output, the pattern must match all filenames to delete (filenames_to_delete) and none of the filenames to keep (filenames_to_keep). The pattern length must equal the length of each filename it matches.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a clause to ensure the pattern is constructed from the filenames_to_delete and filenames_to_keep, and that the pattern is non-empty (if filenames are non-empty). The pattern must be a string of length equal to the filenames it matches, where each character is either a literal or '?' (no other special characters allowed).
candidate_issues.task_evidence: Polycarp wants to run a single delete command with filename pattern as an argument. All the files to be deleted should match the pattern and all other files shouldn't match the pattern. The only special character he knows is a question mark '?' which matches any single character.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a clause to ensure that the pattern is derived from the filenames_to_delete (i.e., it must be possible to construct such a pattern from the intersection of their characters at each position).

candidate_issues.instruction: Replace the expression to ensure the pattern is derived from the filenames_to_delete (i.e., for each position in the pattern, if all filenames_to_delete have the same character at that position, the pattern must use that character; otherwise, it must use '?').
candidate_issues.task_evidence: Formally, a pattern matches a filename if and only if they have equal lengths and all characters in the corresponding positions are equal except when the character in the pattern is '?', in which case the corresponding filename character does not matter.
